doc.title: Frank Wess interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Majesty of the Seas, May 29, 1995

title: Distrust of sound men and Phil Woods's acoustic idea
summary: Wess says you cannot trust sound men and likes Phil Woods's acoustic approach.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Playing for the audience: communicating from the bandstand

blocks.x: Well I tried to make sure that the sound was right before we started. So I went out in the room to hear myself, because that’s another thing, you can’t trust sound men. You can not. I don’t care where they are — Carnegie Hall or anyplace else. You can not trust them because they—
Yeah, which has got nothing to do with—
Or they have their own concept of what they think you sound like.

That’s right. And they don’t know, you know, they really don’t. And then when it gets messed up then they start, you know, or if they get excited by the music they start changing. And they want to take all control. If you want to play soft, they’ll turn you up. You want to play loud, oh, that’s too loud, they turn you down. What the hell is that. Well that’s really I like Phil Wood’s idea of playing acoustic. Then you don’t have to bother with that. But that’s what happens.
